Coating_Composition.Substrate_Material: bond coated button-shaped nickel-based superalloy - IN 738

Process_Text.original: A single-layered APS MSZ coating, system A, was defined as the reference system. A TriplexPro plasma torch with a 9 mm nozzle (Oerlikon Metco), mounted on a six-axis robot in a thermal spray system Multicoat, was used to spray the topcoat.
Process_Text.simplified: Bond-coated IN 738 was cleaned, then single-layer MSZ topcoat was deposited by APS using 500 mm/s robot speed, 200 mm spray distance, and 373 A current.

Ar_He_Ratio_nlpm.Original_Values: Ar/He ratio was maintained at 46 nlpm/4 nlpm

Equipment.Name: F4-VB torch in a LPPS/VPS facility
TriplexPro plasma torch with 9 mm nozzle

Structure_Text.original: Fig. 5(a-c) shows SEM images of the MSZ coating sprayed by the APS system A at different magnifications. The images reveal a lamellar morphology that is well bonded to the substrate, as well as dendritic formations similar to those observed in the original powder. Microcracks were also detected dispersed in the coating. Additionally, isolated and connected voids are present within the coating.
Structure_Text.simplified: APS MZ had a lamellar MSZ coating, dispersed microcracks, isolated and connected voids, and inhomogeneous coating composition.

Coating_Layer_Details.Morphology: lamellar morphology, dendritic formations, microcracks, isolated and connected voids

Raw_Evidence_Span: System B is a double-layered topcoat consisting of an APS YSZ sublayer and an SPS MSZ/MSZ-Ti top layer.
The YSZ sublayer of the double-layer coatings was sprayed with APS using standard methodology to produce a dense layer.
Table 1 Spray parameters for deposition of systems A, B and C.
Table 4 TBC cycle lifetime of two tested specimens.

Process_Text.original: The YSZ sublayer of the double-layer coatings was sprayed with APS using standard methodology to produce a dense layer. After APS deposition, the average thickness of the YSZ layer was about 150 μm. The SPS outer layer was deposited using the Axial III Torch Spray System.
Process_Text.simplified: Dense APS YSZ interlayer was deposited first, followed by SPS MSZ topcoat from 5 wt% MSZ suspension.

Coating_Processing.Deposition_Method: APS YSZ interlayer plus SPS MSZ topcoat

Working_Gas.Value: Ar 75 vol%, H2 15 vol%, N2 10 vol%; total flow 245 SLPM
Working_Gas.Original_Values: Ar (75 vol%), H2 (15 vol%), and N2 (10 vol%) with a total flow rate of 245 standard liters per minute (SLPM)

in-house feeding system developed by Forschungszentrum Jülich

Process_Text.original: The samples were sprayed with a suspension of 5 wt% MSZ or MSZ-7.5TiO2 solids, using the following parameters: a 220 A current, a 140 V voltage, a 92.4 kW power, a 70 mm distance, a 1000 mm/s robot speed, and a calculated net power of 31.1 kW.
Process_Text.simplified: Dense APS YSZ interlayer was deposited first, followed by SPS MSZ-7.5TiO2 topcoat from 5 wt% suspension.

Coating_Processing.Deposition_Method: APS YSZ interlayer plus SPS MSZ-7.5TiO2 topcoat

in-house feeding system developed by Forschungszentrum Jülich

Structure_Text.original: Elemental analysis by EDX shows homogeneous distribution of Mg, Zr, and Ti, especially in coatings prepared with an MSZ7.5TiO2 suspension. Additionally, the addition of TiO2 is not related to any improvement in the microstructure of the coating.
Structure_Text.simplified: DL MZT had a porous columnar SPS MSZ-7.5TiO2 topcoat with homogeneous Mg, Zr, and Ti distribution.

Raw_Evidence_Span: System C uses as-sprayed bond coat substrates that were previously oxidized and coated with an SPS MSZ/MSZ-Ti topcoat.
To produce coatings of system C, the bond-coated substrates were first subjected to a heat treatment in a 99.999 % pure argon atmosphere at 1 atm for two hours at 1140 °C, followed by 16 h at 870 °C.
Table 4 TBC cycle lifetime of two tested specimens.

Composition.Material_Category: pre-oxidized bond-coat magnesia-stabilized zirconia thermal barrier coating

Coating_Composition.Substrate_Material: bond coated button-shaped nickel-based superalloy - IN 738

Coating_Layers.Note: Source text does not state TGO phase composition.

Process_Text.original: The bond-coated substrates were first subjected to a heat treatment in a 99.999 % pure argon atmosphere at 1 atm for two hours at 1140 °C, followed by 16 h at 870 °C. Then, an SPS MSZ layer of approximately 500 μm was sprayed onto the pre-oxidized substrate using the same spray conditions as those used for the aforementioned bi-layered samples.
Process_Text.simplified: Bond-coated IN 738 was pre-oxidized in high-purity argon, then an approximately 500 μm SPS MSZ topcoat was deposited.

in-house feeding system developed by Forschungszentrum Jülich
